A production build of your app needs two values: your deployment's API URL and its anon key. This page shows how each host gets them, and what you see when one is missing.

Pre-1.0: APIs and config may change between releases.

<h2 id="values">What a build needs</h2>

`supatype init`, `supatype dev` and `supatype keys` write a local stack's URL and anon key to `.env.development.local`. Vite, Next.js and Expo read that file in development only, so a production build never ships `localhost`, and gets neither value from it. A production build gets them in one of three ways:

| Way | Use it when |
| --- | --- |
| `supatype build` | You run the build command, on any host. It gives the build both values under every framework's name, and refuses to start without them. |
| `supatype keys --print frontend` | You paste the values into a host's settings. It prints each name and value as a `NAME=value` line. |
| `<script src="/supatype-env.js" vite-ignore>` | Supatype serves the app, or it is a Next.js app with the route [below](#nextjs). The page reads both values from the server when it loads, so one build runs on every deployment that serves it. |

Each framework reads its own names. `supatype build` and `keys --print frontend` give all of them:

| Framework | API URL | Anon key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vite | `VITE_SUPATYPE_URL` | `VITE_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` |
| SvelteKit, Astro | `PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL` | `PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` |
| Next.js | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` |
| Expo | `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL` | `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` |

Pass the values straight to `createClient`, as [Client: Create the client](/docs/client.html#setup) does, with no check of your own in front of it. A bundler that knows a name is unset can turn such a check into a throw that hides the reason. The client checks for itself, and names what is missing.

<h2 id="supatype-build">supatype build</h2>

```sh
$ supatype build                                # runs the package.json build script
$ supatype build -- vite build                  # or the command after --
$ supatype build --env staging -- npm run build # for one linked environment
```

Keep the real build command, such as `vite build`, in package.json's `build` script. A build script that is itself `supatype build` is refused, since a bare `supatype build` runs that script: it stops and says the build script calls `supatype build` itself, so running it again would never end. A command after `--` runs even inside another build.

It runs your build with the deployment's API URL and anon key under all four prefixes. It writes no file: the values live only in the build's environment. The exit code is the build's own, so CI behaves as it did before. Each value is looked for on its own, in this order:

| Source | Where it looks |
| --- | --- |
| The environment | `SUPATYPE_URL` and `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY`, or any of the names above. A host's own settings always win. |
| The server the URL names | For the anon key only, when the environment holds a URL: `<URL>/supatype-env.json`, the key that server publishes. HTTPS for an address that is not local, a local one only with `--allow-local`. A 503 there reads `the server at <url> is not set up to publish its anon key:` and the setting the server names. |
| The linked environment | The one `--env` names, else the link's default. Supatype Cloud: the environment's address, and its anon key from the control plane, which needs `supatype login` (or `SUPATYPE_ACCESS_TOKEN`) as an owner or admin. Self-host: the link's address, and the anon key the server publishes at `/supatype-env.json`, fetched only over HTTPS for an address that is not local. |
| `.env` | `PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL` or `API_EXTERNAL_URL`, and `ANON_KEY`, as the server's own `.env` holds them. |

The first source holding a value decides it. A local address there, such as `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`, stops the build rather than being passed over, because a production build would ship it. Pass `--allow-local` to build against a local stack anyway. A service role key offered as the anon key stops the build too: the service role key never reaches a build. An anon key counts only for the URL being built for: with `SUPATYPE_URL` naming one deployment and a link to another, the link's key is listed as `skipped ... not the URL being built for`, never paired with the wrong address.

`.supatype/link.json` holds secrets and is never committed, so a CI host has no link. There, set `SUPATYPE_URL` in the host's settings: `supatype build` fetches the anon key from `<SUPATYPE_URL>/supatype-env.json`, copies both to every framework's names, and stops the build when one is missing. Set `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` as well only when that server does not publish it (`server.public_env: false`, or a plain `http://` address). `supatype deploy` builds your app with the same values, and takes `--allow-local` too.

<h2 id="supatype-hosts">Supatype hosts it</h2>

When a self-hosted stack serves your app (`app.mode: "static"`), its server answers `/supatype-env.js` with its own address and anon key:

```sh
$ curl https://example.com/supatype-env.js
window.__SUPATYPE_ENV__ = {"url":"https://example.com","anonKey":"eyJhbGciOi..."};
```

`supatype init` puts the tag in a static app's `index.html`, in the head, so it runs before the app's own script. For an app made another way, add it yourself, before the app's own script:

```html title="index.html"
<script src="/supatype-env.js" vite-ignore></script>
<script type="module" src="/src/main.ts"></script>
```

Load it as a plain script, without `async` or `defer`, before the app's own script. A plain script in the head has always run before any module script, wherever the app puts its own; with `async` it can run after it. When it has not run by the client's first request, that request throws, saying the page loads the script but it set no `window.__SUPATYPE_ENV__` in time.

`vite-ignore` tells Vite to leave the tag as it is. The project has no such file, since the server answers it, so without the attribute every `vite build` warns `<script src="/supatype-env.js"> in "/index.html" can't be bundled without type="module" attribute`. Vite drops the attribute from the page it builds, and a browser ignores it, so the same tag does for a page with no build step. Do not make it `type="module"`: Vite then tries to bundle it, and the build fails with `Failed to resolve /supatype-env.js`.

The client reads `window.__SUPATYPE_ENV__` for any value the build did not carry, at its first request. It never guesses the address from the page. A value the build did carry always wins. So a build made with neither value, by a plain `npm run build`, runs on every deployment that serves it. Served from the API's own origin, it needs no [allowed origin](#cors) either. To build on the server instead:

```sh title="vm"
$ supatype app add --static ./dist   # once, then commit supatype.config.ts
$ supatype build                     # reads API_EXTERNAL_URL and ANON_KEY from .env
$ supatype self-host compose up -d
```

:::caution[If the key is missing]
`supatype build` stops before the build starts and lists every source it tried, as shown in [When a value is missing](#missing). A page built without the key and served without the script tag, or by a server with `server.public_env: false`, makes its first request throw in the browser console: `Supatype client has no anon key.`
:::

:::note[Cloud]
For Supatype Cloud, `supatype build --env <name>` and `supatype deploy` read the environment's anon key from the control plane, so a build on a linked machine needs nothing set by hand. Each Cloud environment's API also answers `/supatype-env.json` and `/supatype-env.js` on its own address. On a CI host, use the sections below.
:::

<h2 id="nextjs">Next.js</h2>

A Next.js app does not need its values at build time. `next build` prerenders pages without them, and the route `app/supatype-env.js/route.ts` serves them to each page load from `SUPATYPE_URL` and `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` in the server's environment. `createServerClient` reads the same two, for Server Components, Route Handlers and middleware. `supatype init` writes the route and the root layout's script for an App Router app; [Frameworks: Next.js](/docs/frameworks.html#nextjs) shows both, and the server client. So one build runs on every environment: set the two variables where the app runs. In development the route answers too: `supatype dev`, `init` and `keys --write` put the local stack's `SUPATYPE_URL` and `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` in `.env.development.local`, which `next dev` reads.

| Host | What to set |
| --- | --- |
| Vercel | `SUPATYPE_URL` and `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` under the project's Environment Variables, for each environment. The build command stays `next build`. |
| Netlify | The same two, under the site's Environment variables. |
| Your own Node server | The same two, in the environment of the process that runs `next start`. |

```sh title="vm"
$ npm run build
$ SUPATYPE_URL=https://api.example.com SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY=eyJhbGciOi... npm start
```

`supatype keys --print frontend` prints the values to copy. The route is read on every page load and the server client on every call, so the same build started with another deployment's two values runs against that one. A value fixed into the build under `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL` or `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` still wins over the route's, so leave those unset in production. A Next.js app on its own host or server is on another origin from the API: add its address to the API's allowed origins, as in [Allow your app's origin](#cors). The server client uses them only where `SUPATYPE_URL` or `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` is unset.

A static export (`output: "export"` in `next.config`) has no server to run the route, so `init` writes no route, no layout script and no `@supatype/ssr` for it, and prints the two ways instead: build with the values, `supatype build -- next build`, or have Supatype host the export (`supatype app add --static ./out`), whose server answers `/supatype-env.js` itself; add the `<Script>` tag to the root layout for that.

A Pages Router app gets nothing written by `init`, which prints these steps instead: create the same route file under `app/supatype-env.js/`, beside `pages/`; in `pages/_document.tsx`, import `Script` from `next/script` and put `<Script src="/supatype-env.js" strategy="beforeInteractive" />` inside `<Head>`; add `@supatype/ssr` to the app's dependencies, and set the two variables where it runs.

:::caution[If the key is missing]
The build still succeeds, and the page renders. With `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` or `SUPATYPE_URL` unset, `/supatype-env.js` still answers 200, not cached, but sets only the reason in place of the values: `window.__SUPATYPE_ENV__ = {"error":"public env unavailable: SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY is not set on this server"};`. With both unset it names both, a line each, the key first. It does the same when `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` holds a service role key, and answers 404 only when `SUPATYPE_PUBLIC_ENV` is off. A browser runs no script answered with an error status and tells the page nothing of why, so the reason travels in the script. The browser client's first request then throws `Supatype client has no API address and anon key. createClient was given none, and https://your-app.example.com/supatype-env.js set no API address and anon key, giving the server's reason instead:`, followed by that reason and `Fix that in the environment of the server that answers it`, then the route and the build-time variables. A server client given neither throws on its first request: `Supatype client has no API address and anon key. It was given none, and it is running on a server, where there is no page to read them from.`, followed by `Set SUPATYPE_URL and SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY in the server's environment`.
:::

<h2 id="vercel">Vercel</h2>

Print the values for the deployment on your own machine, where the project is linked:

```sh
$ supatype keys --print frontend --env production
VITE_SUPATYPE_URL=https://api.example.com
PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL=https://api.example.com
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL=https://api.example.com
EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL=https://api.example.com
VITE_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY=eyJhbGciOi...
PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY=eyJhbGciOi...
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY=eyJhbGciOi...
EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY=eyJhbGciOi...
```

In the Vercel project's settings, under Environment Variables, add `SUPATYPE_URL` with that value, for each environment you deploy. `supatype build` fetches the anon key from the server it names; add `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` too if that server does not publish it. Then have Vercel build through the wrapper:

```json title="vercel.json"
{
  "buildCommand": "npx supatype build"
}
```

`supatype build` copies the two values to `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `VITE_` and the other names, then runs your build script. A Next.js app needs no wrapper on Vercel: see [Next.js](#nextjs).

Then allow the site on the API: add its `*.vercel.app` address and any custom domain to the allowed origins, as in [Allow your app's origin](#cors).

:::caution[If the key is missing]
The deployment fails at its build step, before your build starts. The build log shows `No anon key for a production build of the front end.`, each source tried, and ends `or set SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY.`
:::

<h2 id="netlify">Netlify</h2>

Under the site's configuration, in Environment variables, add `SUPATYPE_URL`, and `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` only if the server does not publish its key, with the values `supatype keys --print frontend` prints. Then set the build command:

```toml title="netlify.toml"
[build]
  command = "npx supatype build"
  publish = "dist"
```

`publish` is your build's output directory: `dist` for Vite, `build` for SvelteKit's static adapter. Then add the site's `*.netlify.app` address and any custom domain to the API's allowed origins, as in [Allow your app's origin](#cors).

:::caution[If the key is missing]
The deploy fails in its build step with the same refusal, and nothing is published: the site keeps serving the last deploy that built.
:::

<h2 id="cloudflare">Cloudflare Pages</h2>

In the Pages project's settings:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Build command | `npx supatype build` |
| Build output directory | Your build's output, such as `dist` |
| Variables and Secrets | `SUPATYPE_URL`, from `supatype keys --print frontend`, and `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` only if the server does not publish its key |

Then add the project's `*.pages.dev` address and any custom domain to the API's allowed origins, as in [Allow your app's origin](#cors).

:::caution[If the key is missing]
The build fails, and its log shows the refusal with each source tried. A variable added after the last build reaches only the next one, so retry the deployment once it is set.
:::

<h2 id="github-actions">GitHub Actions</h2>

Store `SUPATYPE_URL` as a repository variable, under Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions. `supatype build` fetches the anon key from the server it names, so a self-hosted deployment needs nothing more: no link and no service role key in CI. Where the server does not publish the key, store `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` too; it is public, so a variable, not a secret, will do.

```yml title=".github/workflows/build.yml"
name: Build

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx supatype build
        env:
          SUPATYPE_URL: ${{ vars.SUPATYPE_URL }}
          # Only where the server does not publish its key:
          # SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY: ${{ vars.SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY }}
```

Publish the output however you deploy it, and add the address it is served from to the API's allowed origins ([Allow your app's origin](#cors)). To give every later step the values under every framework's name instead, run `npx supatype keys --print frontend >> "$GITHUB_ENV"` with the same `env:`. To deploy to your own server over SSH and build there, follow [Deploy to a VM with GitHub Actions](/docs/guides/deploy-vm-github-actions.html).

:::caution[If the key is missing]
The `npx supatype build` step fails and the job stops there. A variable that does not exist reaches the step as an empty string, which counts as not set.
:::

<h2 id="own-server">Your own server</h2>

On the server that runs the stack, `supatype build` needs nothing more: its `.env` records the deployment's `API_EXTERNAL_URL` and `ANON_KEY`.

```sh title="vm"
$ cd /opt/my-app
$ git pull
$ npm install
$ supatype push
$ supatype build
$ supatype self-host compose up -d
```

To build somewhere else, such as your laptop, set `SUPATYPE_URL` to the deployment's address, or link the deployment and name it:

```sh
$ supatype link --env production --url https://api.example.com --token "$SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"
$ supatype build --env production
```

Then copy the output to whatever serves it, and add that server's address to the API's allowed origins ([Allow your app's origin](#cors)); built on the stack's own server and served by it, the app needs nothing. For a self-hosted link the anon key comes from `https://api.example.com/supatype-env.json`. It is fetched over HTTPS only, so a link to a plain `http://` address that is not local gives no key; set `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` instead. A Supatype Cloud link reads the key from the control plane.

:::caution[If the key is missing]
On the server, `anon key from .env: no ANON_KEY` means the keys were never made: run `supatype keys`. `is a local address, which a production build would ship` means `API_EXTERNAL_URL` in `.env` is still a `localhost` address: set it to the server's public one.
:::

<h2 id="cors">Allow your app's origin</h2>

A self-hosted API answers browsers only from the origin of its `SITE_URL` and the origins you list. An app served from anywhere else, such as Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, a Next.js server of its own or a dev server on another port, is refused: the preflight gets 403, and the browser reports `Failed to fetch`. When Supatype serves the app, it is on the API's own origin and needs nothing here.

List the app's origin in `supatype.config.ts`, or in `.env` as `SUPATYPE_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS`, comma-separated. Each entry is `scheme://host[:port]`, with no path:

```ts title="supatype.config.ts"
// supatype.config.ts (excerpt)
api: { corsOrigins: ["https://my-app.vercel.app", "https://www.example.com"] },
```

```ini title=".env"
SUPATYPE_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS=https://my-app.vercel.app,https://www.example.com
```

```sh title="vm"
$ supatype self-host compose restart server
```

The restart renders the compose file again and recreates the server with the new list. Owners, admins and developers can instead add the origin in Studio, on the Settings page's CORS tab, which needs no restart; a list saved there replaces the default until it is reset, and the site URL stays allowed whatever is saved. On Supatype Cloud, add it there. Each preview deployment with its own address is another origin. `supatype dev` allows every origin, so a local stack never shows this. The rest of the rules are under [Self-hosting](/docs/#self-host), in Allowed origins.

<h2 id="missing">When a value is missing</h2>

At build time, `supatype build` stops before the build starts, exits 1, and lists every source it tried for each value. With nothing set, in a project that is not linked:

```sh
$ supatype build
✗ No API URL and no anon key for a production build of the front end.
  not set  API URL from the environment: none of SUPATYPE_URL, VITE_SUPATYPE_URL, PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL, EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL is set
  not set  anon key from the environment: none of SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY, VITE_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY, PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY, EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY is set
  not set  anon key from the server SUPATYPE_URL names: no API URL in the environment to ask
  not set  API URL from the linked environment: no .supatype/link.json (run `supatype link`)
  not set  anon key from the linked environment: no .supatype/link.json (run `supatype link`)
  not set  API URL from .env: no PUBLIC_SUPATYPE_URL or API_EXTERNAL_URL
  not set  anon key from .env: no ANON_KEY

Run `supatype build --env <name>` for a linked deployment, or set SUPATYPE_URL and SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY.
```

The first line starts with `✗` in a terminal, and with `[supatype]` in a CI log or anywhere else the output is not a terminal. With `SUPATYPE_URL` set it starts `No anon key for a production build of the front end.`, and the line for the server the URL names says what that server answered.

`supatype keys --print frontend` reads the same sources, refuses the same way, and names itself as the command to run. It takes `--allow-local` too, for printing a local stack's values: `supatype keys --print frontend --allow-local`. At run time, creating the client never throws, so `next build` can prerender a page that creates one at module scope. The first request a client makes without the anon key throws a `MissingClientValuesError` instead, so the browser console says what is wrong rather than the page going blank. The error starts `Supatype client has no anon key. createClient was given none, and the page had set no window.__SUPATYPE_ENV__ by its first request.` and goes on to name the build-time variables, `supatype build`, the script tag, and for Next.js the route and the server's `SUPATYPE_URL` and `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY`. With no address either, it starts `Supatype client has no API address and anon key.` A page that already loads `/supatype-env.js` is not told to add it. When the server could not give the values, the script sets `error` in their place, and the first request quotes it and sends nothing, on every path: tables, rpc, functions, GraphQL, auth, realtime and storage. When the page has the script element but no `window.__SUPATYPE_ENV__` at all, the script did not run: it was blocked, failed to load, ran after the app's own script, or came from a server too old to serve it. The error says so, and to open the script in the browser to see what it answers.

<h2 id="security">The anon key is public</h2>

The anon key is not a secret. Every browser that loads your app holds it, which is why the server can publish it and a CI host can keep it as a plain variable. What protects your data is the [access rules](/docs/schema.html#access) in your schema, which every request made with the anon key goes through.

The service role key passes every rule, so it never goes near a build. `supatype build` and `keys --print frontend` never output it, and refuse a service role key offered as the anon key. The server never serves it.

`/supatype-env.json` and `/supatype-env.js` are on by default. For an API-only project, with no frontend for the server to serve, turn them off:

```ts title="supatype.config.ts"
// supatype.config.ts (excerpt)
server: {
  public_env: false,
},
```

The next `supatype self-host compose up -d` gives the server `SUPATYPE_PUBLIC_ENV=false`, and both addresses answer 404. A deployment that means to publish and cannot (no anon key, no URL, or a service role key in `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY`) answers `/supatype-env.json` with 503 instead, with no caching and a body naming every setting to fix, and `/supatype-env.js` with 200, not cached, setting only `error` to the same text, which the browser client throws on its first request. `supatype dev` does the same. Turning them off does not make the anon key secret: every client of the API still holds it. It only stops the server publishing it, and `supatype build` for that deployment then needs `SUPATYPE_ANON_KEY` set.
